title: Quotient by distinct linear factors is a product of the coefficient field
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_n\in\Omega$ be pairwise distinct. Put $Q=\prod_{i=1}^n(T-\rho_i)\in\Omega[T]$. Evaluation induces an $\Omega$-algebra isomorphism $\Omega[T]/(Q)\cong\prod_{i=1}^n\Omega$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field), separable polynomial case; Chinese-remainder decomposition into linear factors

proof.text: Index the factors by Fin n; pairwise distinctness makes i ↦ ρ_i injective, so by [lem-pc-crt-pairwise-linear-ideals] the polynomials T - ρ_i are pairwise coprime. Hence [lem-pc-crt-principal-ideal-product] gives ⋂_i (T - ρ_i) = (Q), and the Chinese remainder isomorphism [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] for the pairwise coprime ideals (T - ρ_i) yields a ring isomorphism Ω[T]/(Q) ≅ ∏_i Ω[T]/(T - ρ_i), [f] ↦ ([f] mod (T - ρ_i))_i.

Compose with the product of the evaluation isomorphisms Ω[T]/(T - ρ_i) ≅ Ω, [f] ↦ f(ρ_i), of [lem-pc-crt-linear-evaluation]. The composite Ω[T]/(Q) → ∏_i Ω is the ring isomorphism [f] ↦ (f(ρ_i))_i; it sends the class of a constant c to (c, …, c), so it is Ω-linear, i.e. an Ω-algebra isomorphism.
